text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
- Two out of the three groups within the Socialist Party believe there should be a party conference this year to elect new executives.
- MPs from the Christian Democratic Party will decide whether to quit the party parliamentary group once the party's executives have been elected.
- The chief Hungarian delegate to a session of the North Atlantic Assembly said Sunday Hungary would be willing to host the spring session of the NAA in the year 2000.
- Some 300 notable Hungarians from around the world attended a weekend conference in Parliament on ways to improve Hungary's image abroad.

- Minister for Culture and Education Balint Magyar warned on Sunday that if Parliament passes the school financing agreement with the Vatican in its present form, it could shatter the school system run by local governments.
- Moldavian Prime Minister Ion Ciubuc is due to pay a two-day official visit to Hungary starting on Tuesday, at the invitation of Prime Minister Gyula Horn.

- Police have tracked down a company calling itself the Tax Supervisory Office which early in May sent out 65,000 letters to businesses offering to consider all taxes paid up to December 31, 1995, if they paid 76,000 forints into a specified bank account. (Saturday)
- The real value of the 1998 budget expenditures will not change compared to 1997, Finance Ministry state secretary Laszlo Akar told this daily after Friday's meeting of the economic cabinet.
- The latest World Bank reports points out that excessive foreign investment may be dangerous as they could make the country's industry too dependent on foreign companies.

- The brokerage and the corporate banking arm of ING Hunggary, were profitablelast year, but retail banking activities produced a 730 million loss, retail director Marton Nagy-Gyorgy told the newspaper. (Saturday).
- Agricultrual exporters took up at least three billion forints in unjustified subsidies in the past two and a half year, according to a recent police report.
